title: 更 (gèng) in Chinese: How to Say "Even More" (HSK 3 Grammar)
description: How to use 更 (gèng) for "even more" in Chinese: 更 with adjectives, in 比 sentences and with 喜欢, 更 vs 最, common mistakes and HSK 3 examples.
h1: How to Say "Even More" with 更
lede: 更 (gèng) means "even more" or "-er". Put it before an adjective or a verb like 喜欢 to say that something goes one step further than something else.

paras: 更 always comes directly before the adjective. It usually means the first thing already has the quality and the second has even more of it: if today is cold, tomorrow will be even colder. You can use 更 without 比 when it is clear what you are comparing with.

examples.py: Jīntiān hěn lěng, míngtiān huì gèng lěng.
examples.en: It's cold today, and it'll be even colder tomorrow.

examples.zh: 这件衣服很便宜，那件更便宜。
examples.py: Zhè jiàn yīfu hěn piányi, nà jiàn gèng piányi.
examples.en: This top is cheap, and that one is even cheaper.

examples.zh: 多练习，你的汉语会更好。
examples.py: Duō liànxí, nǐ de Hànyǔ huì gèng hǎo.
examples.en: Practise more and your Chinese will get even better.

paras: A + 比 + B + 更 + adjective.

A plain 比 sentence (他比我高) is already complete. Adding 更 makes it "even taller". The most common mistake is to use 很 instead: 他比我很高 is wrong. You will also hear 还 in the same place, with the same meaning: 他比我还高.

examples.zh: 哥哥很高，弟弟比哥哥更高。
examples.py: Gēge hěn gāo, dìdi bǐ gēge gèng gāo.
examples.en: My older brother is tall, and my younger brother is even taller.

examples.zh: 这个房间比那个房间更大。
examples.py: Zhège fángjiān bǐ nàge fángjiān gèng dà.
examples.en: This room is even bigger than that one.

paras: 更 also goes before verbs of liking, such as 喜欢 and 想. 我更喜欢 is the usual way to say "I prefer". To ask which one someone prefers, use 你更喜欢 with 哪个 or 还是.

examples.zh: 我喜欢喝咖啡，但是我更喜欢喝茶。
examples.py: Wǒ xǐhuan hē kāfēi, dànshì wǒ gèng xǐhuan hē chá.
examples.en: I like coffee, but I like tea even more.

examples.py: Wǒ juéde zhège bànfǎ gèng hǎo.
examples.en: I think this way is better.

paras: 更 compares one thing with another: "more". 最 picks one out of a group: "the most". Both come before the adjective or verb, never after it, and neither is used together with 很: say 我更喜欢, not 我更很喜欢.

examples.zh: 他很高，他哥哥更高，他爸爸最高。
examples.py: Tā hěn gāo, tā gēge gèng gāo, tā bàba zuì gāo.
examples.en: He's tall, his older brother is taller, and his dad is the tallest.

worksheet.title: 更 Worksheet: HSK 3 Printable with Answers
worksheet.description: A free printable 更 (gèng) worksheet for HSK 3: 20 exercises (更, 最 or 很, word order, fix the mistake) with an answer key.

exercises.h2: Choose 更, 最 or 很
exercises.instructions: Write 更, 最 or 很 in each gap. The English tells you what the sentence means.

items.en: This bag is even bigger than that one.
He's the tallest student in our class.
I think Chinese is very interesting.
It was hot yesterday, and today it's even hotter.
This is my favourite dish.
The underground is even quicker than a taxi.
Everything in this shop is very cheap.
He speaks Chinese even better than I do.

items.zh: 苹果和香蕉，你＿＿喜欢哪个？
items.en: Apples or bananas: which do you like better?

items.zh: 我喜欢夏天，但是我＿＿喜欢秋天。
items.en: I like summer, but I like autumn even more.

exercises.instructions: Write the words as one correct sentence.

items.en: It'll be even hotter in the afternoon.
This book is even more interesting than that one.
answers: 这本书比那本更有意思。

items.en: I prefer milk.
This one is even more expensive than that one.
My younger sister is even taller than me.

exercises.instructions: Each sentence has one mistake. Write the correct sentence.

items.en: He's even taller than me.
Today is even hotter than yesterday.
This dish is even tastier than that one.
I like this one even more.
Do you prefer cats or dogs?
